title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 56
paragraphs: The vision in Hipparchus's dream was this. On the night before the Panathenaea, it seemed to Hipparchus that a man came and stood by him, tall and of fair form, and riddling spoke these verses to him:
“With enduring soul, as a lion, endure unendurable evil: no man who does wrong shall escape the appointed judgment.”

As soon as it was day, he publicly communicated these verses to the interpreters of dreams; but afterwards he dismissed the vision from his mind and began to take part in that procession in which he lost his life.
